NO. 036 · Wetlands & Waterways / Anatidae · Ducks

Eurasian Teal

绿翅鸭 · lǜ chì yā Anas crecca
Winter visitor Common 34–38 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The commonest small wild duck in South China

Half the size of a domestic duck, and it leaves the water almost vertically. The drake wears a dark green mask from eye to nape, a horizontal white line along the flank and a bright yellow triangle at the tail — a remarkably neat piece of design.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • MaleHead chestnut-brown with a broad dark green mask running back from the eye; body grey and finely vermiculated, with a bold horizontal white line along the flank.
  • FlanksA bright yellow triangular patch on each side at the base of the tail — the quickest way to identify a drake.
  • FemaleBrown and mottled all over, a small orange-red patch at the base of the bill, and a green speculum on the wing — 'green-winged' refers to the speculum both sexes share.
  • ShapeSmall and compact, neck short, tail slightly cocked when afloat.

Behaviour

The commonest wintering duck in South China, feeding on the water in flocks of tens to hundreds, taking aquatic seeds and algae and flying out to rice fields and shallows at dusk. It needs no run-up: it springs straight off the surface, and fast.

Voice

The drake gives a clear whistled 'krik', the duck a low quack; calls run continuously through a flying flock.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen fish ponds
  • Qianwu Reservoir
  • Jinwan wetlands
  • Hengqin waterways
Field note
A party of small ducks that seems to be catapulted off the water is almost certainly this species. Look for the yellow triangle beside the tail and the green mask on the drake.
